cd my-project

npm run dev
```

### Create and start a Vite dev server with createServer

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/api-javascript.md

Initializes, starts, and prints URLs for a Vite development server programmatically with custom port and root configurations.

```ts
import { createServer } from 'vite'

const server = await createServer({
  // any valid user config options, plus `mode` and `configFile`
  configFile: false,
  root: import.meta.dirname,
  server: {
    port: 1337,
  },
})
await server.listen()

server.printUrls()
server.bindCLIShortcuts({ print: true })
```

### configurePreviewServer

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/api-plugin.md

Configures the Vite preview server instance. Called before internal middlewares are installed, with support for returning a post-hook callback to install middlewares afterward.

```APIDOC
### configurePreviewServer

#### Signature
`(server: PreviewServer) => (() => void) | void | Promise<(() => void) | void>`

#### Parameters
- `server` (`PreviewServer`) - The preview server instance.

#### Returns
- `(() => void) | void | Promise<(() => void) | void>` - Optionally returns a function called after internal middlewares are installed.

#### Details
- **Kind:** `async`, `sequential`
- **Scope:** Global
- Hook is called before other middlewares are installed. Return a post hook callback function if middleware should be injected after internal middlewares.

#### Example
```js
const myPlugin = () => ({
  name: 'configure-preview-server',
  configurePreviewServer(server) {
    // return a post hook that is called after other middlewares are installed
    return () => {
      server.middlewares.use((req, res, next) => {
        // custom handle request...
      })
    }
  },
})
```
```

### Preview production build with vite preview

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/cli.md

Locally previews the production build by starting a server in the build directory. Run vite build beforehand to ensure the output directory is up-to-date.

```bash
vite preview [root]
```

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/config/server-options.md

export default defineConfig({

    open: '/docs/index.html',
  },
})

### Start Vite dev server with CPU profiling

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/troubleshooting.md

Use this command to start the Vite dev server with the built-in Node.js inspector and automatically open the browser. After the app loads, press p to stop the inspector and q to stop the dev server. The inspector generates vite-profile-0.cpuprofile in the root folder.

```bash
vite --profile --open
```

### Example .vite/manifest.json structure

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/backend-integration.md

Output generated in outDir after running vite build when manifest is enabled, mapping source entries to output assets and dependencies.

```json
{
  "_shared-B7PI925R.js": {
    "file": "assets/shared-B7PI925R.js",
    "name": "shared",
    "css": ["assets/shared-ChJ_j-JJ.css"]
  },
  "_shared-ChJ_j-JJ.css": {
    "file": "assets/shared-ChJ_j-JJ.css",
    "src": "_shared-ChJ_j-JJ.css"
  },
  "logo.svg": {
    "file": "assets/logo-BuPIv-2h.svg",
    "src": "logo.svg"
  },
  "baz.js": {
    "file": "assets/baz-B2H3sXNv.js",
    "name": "baz",
    "src": "baz.js",
    "isDynamicEntry": true
  },
  "views/bar.js": {
    "file": "assets/bar-gkvgaI9m.js",
    "name": "bar",
    "src": "views/bar.js",
    "isEntry": true,
    "imports": ["_shared-B7PI925R.js"],
    "dynamicImports": ["baz.js"]
  },
  "views/foo.js": {
    "file": "assets/foo-BRBmoGS9.js",
    "name": "foo",
    "src": "views/foo.js",
    "isEntry": true,
    "imports": ["_shared-B7PI925R.js"],
    "css": ["assets/foo-5UjPuW-k.css"]
  }
}
```

const module = await import(`./dir/${file}.js`)

### Access WebAssembly Module via URL import

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/features.md

Uses the ?url query suffix to get the resolved asset URL for explicit instantiation using WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming.

```js
import 'vite/client'
// ---cut---
import wasmUrl from 'foo.wasm?url'

const main = async () => {
  const responsePromise = fetch(wasmUrl)
  const { module, instance } =
    await WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(responsePromise)
  /* ... */
}

main()
```

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/playground/resolve/index.html

Imports from packages that test exports environment, exports from root, legacy fallback, and exports with module field. Tests various exports field conditions.

```javascript
import { msg as exportsEnvMsg } from '@vitejs/test-resolve-exports-env' text('.exports-env', exportsEnvMsg) import { msg as exportsFromRootMsg } from '@vitejs/test-resolve-exports-from-root/nested' text('.exports-from-root', exportsFromRootMsg) import { msg as exportsLegacyFallbackMsg } from '@vitejs/test-resolve-exports-legacy-fallback/dir' text('.exports-legacy-fallback', exportsLegacyFallbackMsg) import { msg as exportsWithModule } from '@vitejs/test-resolve-exports-with-module' text('.exports-with-module', exportsWithModule)
```

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/performance.md

```bash
vite:transform 28.72ms /@vite/client +1ms
vite:transform 62.95ms /src/components/BigComponent.vue +1ms
vite:transform 102.54ms /src/utils/big-utils.js +1ms
```

// exports field import { msg } from '@vitejs/test-resolve-exports-path' text('.exports-entry', msg) // deep import w/ exports import { msg as deepMsg } from '@vitejs/test-resolve-exports-path/deep.js' text('.exports-deep', deepMsg) // deep import w/ exports w/ query import deepPath from '@vitejs/test-resolve-exports-path/deep.json?url' text('.exports-deep-query', deepPath) // deep import w/ exposed dir import { msg as exposedDirMsg } from '@vitejs/test-resolve-exports-path/dir/dir' text('.exports-deep-exposed-dir', exposedDirMsg) // deep import w/ mapped dir import { msg as mappedDirMsg } from '@vitejs/test-resolve-exports-path/dir-mapped/dir' text('.exports-deep-mapped-dir', mappedDirMsg)

### Import and initialize WebAssembly modules using ?init

import init from './example.wasm?init'

init().then((instance) => {
  instance.exports.test()
})

### Import from UTF-8 BOM file and deep import with @babel/runtime

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/playground/resolve/index.html

Imports a message from a UTF-8 BOM file and uses @babel/runtime to slice an iterable. The BOM file import tests handling of byte order marks.

```javascript
import '@generated-content-virtual-file' function text(selector, text) { document.querySelector(selector).textContent = text } // import from a utf-8 bom file import { msg as bomMsg } from './utf8-bom/main.js' text('.utf8-bom', bomMsg) // deep import import slicedToArray from '@babel/runtime/helpers/esm/slicedToArray' const iterable = (function\* () { yield 2 yield 4 yield 6 yield 8 })() text('.deep-import', JSON.stringify(slicedToArray(iterable, 2)))
```

### Install trusted SSL certificate on macOS

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/troubleshooting.md

Use this on macOS to install a trusted SSL certificate via the CLI, resolving network request issues caused by self-signed certificates. Replace your-cert.cer with the actual certificate file.

```shell
security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k ~/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db your-cert.cer
```

### Configure multiple HTML entry points for multi-page build

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/build.md

Specify multiple `.html` files as entry points in `vite.config.js` using `input` mappings.

```javascript
import { resolve } from 'node:path'
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'

export default defineConfig({
  input: {
    main: resolve(import.meta.dirname, 'index.html'),
    nested: resolve(import.meta.dirname, 'nested/index.html'),
  },
})
```

### Overview of .env file loading hierarchy

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/env-and-mode.md

Lists the standard .env filenames Vite loads depending on the current mode and local override status.

```text
.env                # loaded in all cases
.env.local          # loaded in all cases, ignored by git
.env.[mode]         # only loaded in specified mode
.env.[mode].local   # only loaded in specified mode, ignored by git
```

```bash

```.env.staging
VITE_APP_TITLE=My App (staging)
```

### Inject post-middleware via configureServer hook

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/api-plugin.md

Return a function from configureServer to register custom middlewares that execute after internal middlewares are installed.

```javascript
const myPlugin = () => ({
  name: 'configure-server',
  configureServer(server) {
    // return a post hook that is called after internal middlewares are
    // installed
    return () => {
      server.middlewares.use((req, res, next) => {
        // custom handle request...
      })
    }
  },
})
```

--------------------------------

### Attach pre-middleware via configureServer hook

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/api-plugin.md

Adds custom middlewares to the Vite connect application that execute before internal middlewares are installed.

```javascript
const myPlugin = () => ({
  name: 'configure-server',
  configureServer(server) {
    server.middlewares.use((req, res, next) => {
      // custom handle request...
    })
  },
})
```

--------------------------------

### Instantiate and execute code using ModuleRunner

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/api-environment-runtimes.md

Demonstrates initializing a `ModuleRunner` with an RPC transport and `ESModulesEvaluator` before executing an entry-point module.

```javascript
import {
  ModuleRunner,
  ESModulesEvaluator,
  createNodeImportMeta,
} from 'vite/module-runner'
import { transport } from './rpc-implementation.js'

const moduleRunner = new ModuleRunner(
  {
    transport,
    createImportMeta: createNodeImportMeta, // if the module runner runs in Node.js
  },
  new ESModulesEvaluator(),
)

await moduleRunner.import('/src/entry-point.js')
```

--------------------------------

### Configure server.warmup in Vite config

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/config/server-options.md

Specify client and SSR files or glob patterns to pre-transform and cache on server startup to improve initial load performance.

```js
export default defineConfig({
  server: {
    warmup: {
      clientFiles: ['./src/components/*.vue', './src/utils/big-utils.js'],
      ssrFiles: ['./src/server/modules/*.js'],
    },
  },
})
```

--------------------------------

### Configure type-aware lint rules in .oxlintrc.json

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/packages/create-vite/template-react-ts/README.md

Enables type-aware linting with the react, typescript, and oxc plugins in .oxlintrc.json for production applications after installing oxlint-tsgolint.

```json
{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/oxlint/configuration_schema.json",
  "plugins": ["react", "typescript", "oxc"],
  "options": {
    "typeAware": true
  },
  "rules": {
    "react/rules-of-hooks": "error",
    "react/only-export-components": ["warn", { "allowConstantExport": true }]
  }
}
```

--------------------------------

### createFetchableDevEnvironment(name, config, options)

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/api-environment-frameworks.md

Creates a FetchableDevEnvironment instance that communicates with its runtime via the Fetch API. Useful for runtimes that cannot run Vite directly.

```APIDOC
### createFetchableDevEnvironment(name, config, options)

Creates a new `FetchableDevEnvironment` instance configured with a request handler.

#### Parameters
- **name** (`string`) - Environment name.
- **config** (`ResolvedConfig`) - The resolved Vite configuration.
- **options** (`object`)
  - **handleRequest** (`(request: Request) => Promise<Response> | Response`) - Required function to handle incoming `Request` objects and return a `Response`.

#### Returns
- `FetchableDevEnvironment` - The created fetchable dev environment instance.
```

### Installing and registering @vitejs/plugin-legacy

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/using-plugins.md

Add a plugin to devDependencies and include it in the plugins array inside vite.config.js. Vite accepts presets as nested arrays and automatically flattens them, ignoring any falsy plugin values.

```bash
$ npm add -D @vitejs/plugin-legacy
```

```javascript
import legacy from '@vitejs/plugin-legacy'
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    legacy({
      targets: ['defaults', 'not IE 11'],
    }),
  ],
})
```

import { msg as exportsWithModuleCondition } from '@vitejs/test-resolve-exports-with-module-condition' import { msg as exportsWithModuleConditionRequired } from '@vitejs/test-resolve-exports-with-module-condition-required' text('.exports-with-module-condition', exportsWithModuleCondition) text( '.exports-with-module-condition-required', exportsWithModuleConditionRequired, )

### Configure build.lib for multiple entries in vite.config.js

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/build.md

Specify an object in `build.lib.entry` to support bundling multiple entry points for a library.

```js
import { resolve } from 'node:path'
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'

export default defineConfig({
  build: {
    lib: {
      entry: {
        'my-lib': resolve(import.meta.dirname, 'lib/main.js'),
        secondary: resolve(import.meta.dirname, 'lib/secondary.js'),
      },
      name: 'MyLib',
    },
    rolldownOptions: {
      // make sure to externalize deps that shouldn't be bundled
      // into your library
      external: ['vue'],
      output: {
        // Provide global variables to use in the UMD build
        // for externalized deps
        globals: {
          vue: 'Vue',
        },
      },
    },
  },
})
```

### Render production asset links from manifest template

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/backend-integration.md

Demonstrates the pseudo-template logic for rendering production `<link>` and `<script>` tags from the manifest. Follow this loading order for optimal performance when creating server-side templates.

```html
<!-- if production -->

<!-- for cssFile of manifest[name].css -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/{{ cssFile }}" />

<!-- for chunk of importedChunks(manifest, name) -->
<!-- for cssFile of chunk.css -->
<link rel="stylesheet" href="/{{ cssFile }}" />

<script type="module" src="/{{ manifest[name].file }}"></script>

<!-- for chunk of importedChunks(manifest, name) -->
<link rel="modulepreload" href="/{{ chunk.file }}" />
```

### createServer(inlineConfig?)

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/api-javascript.md

Creates a Vite development server instance programmatically. It accepts an optional configuration object and returns a promise resolving to a ViteDevServer.

```APIDOC
## createServer

### Description
Creates a Vite development server instance programmatically.

### Type Signature
```ts
async function createServer(inlineConfig?: InlineConfig): Promise<ViteDevServer>
```

### Parameters
- **inlineConfig** (`InlineConfig`, optional) - Any valid user configuration options, plus `mode` and `configFile`.

### Returns
- `Promise<ViteDevServer>` - Resolves to the created development server instance.

### Usage Example
```ts
import { createServer } from 'vite'

const server = await createServer({
  // any valid user config options, plus `mode` and `configFile`
  configFile: false,
  root: import.meta.dirname,
  server: {
    port: 1337,
  },
})
await server.listen()

server.printUrls()
server.bindCLIShortcuts({ print: true })
```

### Middleware Mode Example with WebSocket Proxy
```ts
import http from 'http'
import { createServer } from 'vite'

const parentServer = http.createServer() // or express, koa, etc.

const vite = await createServer({
  server: {
    // Enable middleware mode
    middlewareMode: {
      // Provide the parent http server for proxy WebSocket
      server: parentServer,
    },
    proxy: {
      '/ws': {
        target: 'ws://localhost:3000',
        // Proxying WebSocket
        ws: true,
      },
    },
  },
})

parentServer.use(vite.middlewares)
```
```

### Fix HMR by correcting import case in src/bar.js

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/troubleshooting.md

Use this when Vite detects a file change but HMR is not working. The import path case must match the actual file name; for example, if src/foo.js exists, import './foo.js' instead of './Foo.js'.

```js
import './Foo.js' // should be './foo.js'
```

### Configure basic experimental.renderBuiltUrl for runtime and relative URLs

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/build.md

Use `experimental.renderBuiltUrl` to customize asset URLs based on `hostType`, returning dynamic runtime expressions or relative paths.

```ts
import type { UserConfig } from 'vite'
// prettier-ignore
const config: UserConfig = {
// ---cut-before---
experimental: {
  renderBuiltUrl(filename, { hostType }) {
    if (hostType === 'js') {
      return { runtime: `window.__toCdnUrl(${JSON.stringify(filename)})` }
    } else {
      return { relative: true }
    }
  },
},
// ---cut-after---
}
```

### Import from imports field with various patterns

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/playground/resolve/index.html

Imports from packages using the imports field with top-level, same-level, nested, star, star-dollar, slash, pkg-slash, query, dot-prefixed, root-slash, double-hash, mid-hash, question-mark, hash-hash, hash-query, mid-hash-postfix, and question-mark-postfix patterns. Tests imports field resolution.

```javascript
// imports field import { msg as importsTopLevel } from '#top-level' text('.imports-top-level', importsTopLevel) import { msg as importsSameLevel } from '#same-level' text('.imports-same-level', importsSameLevel) import { msg as importsNested } from '#nested/path.js' text('.imports-nested', importsNested) import { msg as importsStar } from '#star/index.js' text('.imports-star', importsStar) import { msg as importsStarDollar } from '#star/dollar$$.js' text('.imports-star-dollar', importsStarDollar) import { msg as importsSlash } from '#slash/index.js' text('.imports-slash', importsSlash) import { msg as importsPkgSlash } from '#other-pkg-slash/index.js' text('.imports-pkg-slash', importsPkgSlash) import importsQuery from '#query?url' text('.imports-query', importsQuery) import { msg as importsDotPrefixed } from './imports-path/importer.js' text('.imports-dot-prefixed', importsDotPrefixed) import { msg as importsRootSlash } from '#/index.js' text('.imports-root-slash', importsRootSlash) import { msg as importsDoubleHash } from '##double/index.js' text('.imports-double-hash', importsDoubleHash) import { msg as importsMidHash } from '#mid#hash' text('.imports-mid-hash', importsMidHash) import { msg as importsQuestionMark } from '#question?mark' text('.imports-question-mark', importsQuestionMark) import { msg as importsHashHash } from './imports-path/importer-hash-hash.js' text('.imports-hash-hash', importsHashHash) import { msg as importsHashQuery } from '#hash?query' text('.imports-hash-query', importsHashQuery) import { msg as importsMidHashPostfix } from '#mid#hash#fragment?query' text('.imports-mid-hash-postfix', importsMidHashPostfix) import { msg as importsQuestionMarkPostfix } from '#question?mark?query#fragment' text('.imports-question-mark-postfix', importsQuestionMarkPostfix)

### Typical SSR application source file structure

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/ssr.md

Shows the recommended directory and file layout for an SSR application, including server, universal code, client entry, and server entry files.

```text
- index.html
- server.js # main application server
- src/
  - main.js          # exports env-agnostic (universal) app code
  - entry-client.js  # mounts the app to a DOM element
  - entry-server.js  # renders the app using the framework's SSR API
```

import './global.css' // Importing a file outside the `root` should provide an @fs path. import outsideRootUrl from '~/images/logo.png' setAssetReference('.outside-root', outsideRootUrl) // Helper: Allows to test the URL content as well as the request being served. function setAssetReference(elSelector, url) { const text = document.createElement('code') text.classList.add('asset-url') text.textContent = url const img = document.createElement('img') img.classList.add('asset-preview') img.src = url const el = document.querySelector(`.asset-reference${elSelector}`) el.appendChild(img) el.appendChild(text) }

### Configure build.lib for single entry in vite.config.js

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/build.md

Use `build.lib` to bundle a single entry library, externalizing dependencies like `vue` and providing UMD globals.

```js
import { resolve } from 'node:path'
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'

export default defineConfig({
  build: {
    lib: {
      entry: resolve(import.meta.dirname, 'lib/main.js'),
      name: 'MyLib',
      // the proper extensions will be added
      fileName: 'my-lib',
    },
    rolldownOptions: {
      // make sure to externalize deps that shouldn't be bundled
      // into your library
      external: ['vue'],
      output: {
        // Provide global variables to use in the UMD build
        // for externalized deps
        globals: {
          vue: 'Vue',
        },
      },
    },
  },
})
```

--------------------------------

### Configure server.fs.allow to serve files from parent directory

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/config/server-options.md

Specifies directory paths allowed for serving via /@fs/. Accepts absolute paths or paths relative to the project root.

```javascript
export default defineConfig({
  server: {
    fs: {
      // Allow serving files from one level up to the project root
      allow: ['..'],
    },
  },
})
```

### Inject license reference banner via build.rolldownOptions

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/config/build-options.md

Enables `build.license` and uses `build.rolldownOptions.output.postBanner` to insert a comment referencing the license file at the top of bundled files.

```javascript
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'

export default defineConfig({
  build: {
    license: true,
    rolldownOptions: {
      output: {
        postBanner:
          '/* See licenses of bundled dependencies at https://example.com/license.md */',
      },
    },
  },
})
```

--------------------------------

### Configuring and Dispatching Requests with FetchableDevEnvironment

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/api-environment-frameworks.md

Create a custom fetchable environment with `createFetchableDevEnvironment` and process requests using `dispatchFetch`. Vite strictly requires inputs and outputs to be instances of the global `Request` and `Response` classes, throwing a `TypeError` otherwise.

```ts
import {
  createServer,
  createFetchableDevEnvironment,
  isFetchableDevEnvironment,
} from 'vite'

const server = await createServer({
  server: { middlewareMode: true },
  appType: 'custom',
  environments: {
    custom: {
      dev: {
        createEnvironment(name, config) {
          return createFetchableDevEnvironment(name, config, {
            handleRequest(request: Request): Promise<Response> | Response {
              // handle Request and return a Response
            },
          })
        },
      },
    },
  },
})

// Any consumer of the environment API can now call `dispatchFetch`
if (isFetchableDevEnvironment(server.environments.custom)) {
  const response: Response = await server.environments.custom.dispatchFetch(
    new Request('http://example.com/request-to-handle'),
  )
}
```

Explicitly define a custom configuration file path resolved relative to the current working directory.

### Configure server.warmup in vite.config.js

Source: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/main/docs/guide/performance.md

Pre-transforms and caches specified client files before browser requests arrive. Only frequently used files should be included to avoid overloading the Vite dev server during startup.

```javascript
export default defineConfig({
  server: {
    warmup: {
      clientFiles: [
        './src/components/BigComponent.vue',
        './src/utils/big-utils.js',
      ],
    },
  },
})
```
